pairs.why: Both are very close, but A's flames, logs and stones are a bit crisper and more saturated, like the clean cartoon finish of the real pot and dock cards, while B is slightly flatter and duller.
B's logs glow more warmly and its surfaces are a little smoother, which fits the lessons' preference for smooth over textured, though the gap between A and B is small.
B looks soft and clay-like, close to the over-smooth extreme, while A keeps the crisp edges and moderate surface detail of the real cards.
A's stones and flame are softened almost to blur, while B keeps defined forms and saturated, punchy color closer to the real cards.
B is the softer, mushier render, while A shows crisp but not gritty detail, closer to the real cards' smooth-but-defined finish.
A has the same over-softened clay look as the other left-cabin version, while B's stones, logs and flame read cleaner and more defined, like the real cards.
